title: ConsensusCourt: Procedural Evidence Arbitration for Scientific Claims in Multi-Agent Research Pipelines (v0.4.17)

creators.name: Wang, Wei
creators.affiliation: Shanghai Hongene Biologics Tech Co., Ltd.

description:
Open-source companion to the preprint ConsensusCourt: Procedural Evidence Arbitration for Scientific Claims in Multi-Agent Research Pipelines (v0.4.17, September 21, 2026). Contains the manuscript sources and compiled PDF (paper/), the court/baseline/rubric implementations under test (code/core/), one deterministic experiment pipeline per paper table and figure (code/scripts/), the pytest suites and DDB benchmark generators (code/tests/), and every machine-readable report backing the manuscript's numbers (code/data/).

ConsensusCourt borrows its procedural guarantees from the courtroom rather than voting theory: an asymmetric burden of proof (claims are presumed innocent until a detected contradiction pair convicts them), a source-pedigree evidence scorer whose confidence channel is structurally decoupled from conviction, a three-state (pass/fail/unknown) citation-verification policy that holds the clean-claim false-positive rate at 0 under verification failure rates up to 100%, and an escalation layer routing unadjudicable cases to human review.

The benchmark and red-line experiments are deterministic (seed = 42) and zero-LLM; entry point: run_v03_regression.sh. Code, tests, and data are MIT-licensed; the manuscript under paper/ is All Rights Reserved (arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license selected at submission).
